data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold. The RP2354B stays for "Microcontroller". The stock verifier confirms the part and refutes nothing: its refutation text is empty and all 14 of its checks pass. The datasheet verifier fails 3 checks: watchdog stall cover (V2), watchdog window (V1 and V2), and image watchdog timeout (V4). The verifier itself says each one fails on the firmware, not on the part. I re-read the sources and agree.

(1) What the part can do. RP2350 datasheet Table 1249 (LOAD, bits 23:0) allows any timeout up to 0xffffff us, which is 16,777,215 us or about 16.8 s. CTRL.ENABLE resets to 0 (Table 1248), so firmware turns the watchdog on. Any timeout under V1's 500 ms can be set. So can any timeout above the 400 ms packaged-part maximum for a W25Q16JV sector erase. The window between 400 ms and 500 ms, less the reset time, exists on this part. The datasheet does not state the time from expiry to the pads reaching their reset state. That time is not read.

(2) V2, the stall. The 900 ms figure is one 400 ms erase followed by a console write in the same main-loop pass (main.c:1049-1089). With a slow host the stall has no bound. In pico-sdk 2.3.0, stdio_usb_out_chars() sets last_avail_time after every chunk the host accepts (stdio_usb.c:118). It gives up only after PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US with nothing accepted (stdio_usb.c:122). That constant is 500,000 us by default, and the build can override it (stdio_usb.h:31-33). Both the erase in the loop and the console write are firmware choices. The firmware can move the store: Q8 is decided, and the output binding moves to the MB85RC256VPNF-G-AMERE2 FRAM (owner, 2026-09-29). It can also cap the console write. No microcontroller's watchdog can cover a stall with no bound. The part does not cause that stall.

(3) V4, the timeout the image sets. Searching firmware/iomcu/ for "watchdog" finds only the comment at main.c:970-973, with no watchdog_enable() or watchdog_update(). So the image sets no timeout. That is the value found for V4. It is a gap in the firmware, not a datasheet value. The specification already records it: IOBoard.md:251 says "The image enables none". hardware/STATUS.md:76 lists the timeout, the console-write cap and the move of the store to the FRAM as firmware work.

This is the third time the same question has come up. FU-A4 adjudicator-R1 (007) ruled the same way on the same three watchdog checks: not a property of the part.

The RP2354B is also a fixed input. Under Research.md Scope, a fixed input is checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source. One that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. The watchdog findings go to the owner and to firmware as findings: there is no timeout in the image, and the console-write cap is not stated.

Part-level facts I re-read all pass:
- JLCPCB C39843328 is RP2354B, Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), erpComponentName SC1512(13)-A4. stockCount is 2535, which passes the gate of 50 (max(5 x 10, 50)). canPresaleNumber is 2418.
- The Raspberry Pi PCN (product change notice) listing still holds only "RP235x A4 stepping PCN". That notice ends the steppings other than A4. It is not an end-of-life notice for the A4 part.
- 20 held parts cover the need of 10: 5 boards x 2 a board.
- Raspberry Pi is on the S1 allowlist.
data.evidence:
RP2350 datasheet, build 2025-07-29 (SHA-256 2877d0f270fb6d6a57943bee58aaad536aa027bea1e5b1c4ce2541a3230d4be8), served by datasheets.raspberrypi.com and redirected to pip-assets.raspberrypi.com, read 2026-10-01T22:24:26Z. Table 1249 LOAD 23:0: "Load the watchdog timer. The maximum setting is 0xffffff which corresponds to approximately 16 seconds." Table 1248 CTRL: TIME 23:0 is in usec, and ENABLE resets to 0.

pico-sdk 2.3.0 stdio_usb.c (SHA-256 d1ca4298b9142210aaa40dffe08d4bbefb13adccbba0f63b2c4072cb4a25eaab), read 2026-10-01T22:24:42Z. Line 118 sets last_avail_time = time_us_64() after each accepted chunk. Line 122 breaks only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed. stdio_usb.h:31-33 defines that constant as 500000 by default and lets the build override it.

Checkout 08042b06b2dc:
- grep -rn -i watchdog firmware/iomcu/ finds only main.c:970-973, a comment.
- No PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US override exists under firmware/ or shared/.
- main.c:1049-1089: an erase or program step of out_store_tick, then a printf in the same pass.
- IOBoard.md:251: "The stop deadline it serves is 500 ms (owner, 2026-09-30); the watchdog timeout is not stated ... The image enables none."
- STATUS.md:76, next step: "the timeout, the console-write cap and the move of the output store to the FRAM, in firmware".
- Research.md: V1 is 500 ms (owner, 2026-09-30). V2 and V4 are for research. Q8 is the I2C FRAM MB85RC256VPNF-G-AMERE2 (owner, 2026-09-29). Scope: "A fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected."

Precedent: round1/FU-A4/007-adjudicator-R1.json, stands false, scope function, on the same watchdog checks.

JLCPCB C39843328, read 2026-10-01T22:24:47Z: RP2354B, Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), SC1512(13)-A4, stockCount 2535, canPresaleNumber 2418, expand.

PCN listing, read 2026-10-01T22:24:52Z, HTTP 200: one entry, "RP235x A4 stepping PCN", updated 6 Oct 2025.

The time from watchdog expiry to the pads reaching their reset state is not read. The datasheet does not state it.
